title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real contrast was not executed and that the confirmatory estimand executed here is the paired guarded−baseline difference on the synthetic/emulation partition. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation however creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the *same* initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. We executed N_pairs = 250 intents on a synthetic/emulation partition; results, execution accounting, representative artifacts, and analysis logs are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and empirical evaluations position intent-driven LLM configuration generation and the verification requirement as active research topics; representative studies include NetConfEval and several recent reviews of LLMs for NetOps that motivate generate–verify flows [1],[2],[5]. Prior work on deterministic verification and formal-analysis tools (e.g., Batfish-style reachability/policy checking, header-space methods, and model-checking variants) provides mature mechanisms for mechanically verifying forwarding and local-policy properties and has been integrated as validator components in GVR pipelines [3],[6].

Research in generate-and-verify program repair and configuration repair demonstrates that deterministic checks plus template-driven repairs can remove mechanically verifiable defects in code and config domains, yet those evaluations typically emphasize syntactic/locally-checkable errors and note limits for richer semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties [4],[7]. Security analyses of prompt-injection emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but also show that adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved threat in operational deployments [8]. Our study contributes by quantifying the marginal verifier-detected benefit under shared_initial_candidate semantics on a constrained synthetic partition and by making provider-call accounting and reconciliation explicit and auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1. The preregistration specified a paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede; this preregistration froze inclusion/exclusion rules, the single-repair policy, the analysis plan (exact McNemar two-sided and paired bootstrap CI), and the maximum model-call budget.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (clarification). Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded). No independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. This design therefore isolates the marginal effect of deterministic validation and the single permitted repair on an identical candidate rather than measuring differences arising from distinct generated candidates. Provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation of stage counts are archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, sha256 = 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3) and document how the single generation per intent plus the single repair call reconcile to the completed episodes and model-call totals.

Task generation, model, and guarded pipeline. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks (intent templates, expected sequences, and allowed_touched_fields). The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; provider recorded as openai_responses). For each intent we executed one shared initial generation (the shared candidate). Per intent we then executed two deterministic validator evaluations (one under baseline acceptance semantics and one under guarded semantics that invoked the same validator): baseline — accept the shared candidate as-is and submit it to the deterministic validator for scoring; guarded — submit the same shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, if the validator failed, permit up to one automated repair call using preregistered repair templates. Repairs were restricted to the preregistered, template-driven transformation attempts only; no iterative repair beyond the single allowed attempt was permitted.

Deterministic validator and scoring. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performed full_intent_constraint_validation: it parsed generated CLI sequences, counted parsed_command_count, verified required_sequence ordering and workflow constraints, and compared final_state snapshots to the expected_final_state encoded in the task payload. Validator traces for passed and failed episodes include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, listed violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag. Representative validator-scored artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256 = 2e5c4b8b0b140177365a4a6e346762ac54a123fac7e180c3e47a485ba16a8e61) and the paired guarded record execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256 = 5a61c1d1299e52a2b3d90fefe06c173f41299cd6977c42de060e239fd6fc927a).

Provider-call accounting and reconciliation (clarification). The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (251 = 250 shared initial_generation calls + 1 repair). The provider_call_audit included in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json reports stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 251; condition_counts appear instrumented as {"shared":250,"guarded":1} in the adapter labeling but the reconciliation artifact shows that all completed episodes derive from the 250 shared initial candidates plus the single permitted repair call. The reconciliation artifact and provider_call_audit are the authoritative reconciliation sources for model-call accounting and stage mapping (see analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, sha256 given above).

Confirmatory analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is a two-sided exact McNemar test on the paired binary outcomes with paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor implemented the paired_binary_analysis_v1 contract; analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256 = 087550a3a6a9e656df95062b9779244de2793931b906af1d06a1c79f8073beb2) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256 = 2de9aaf722ec5a51530c8bb6e4930592db24786e18fc6c9574a7e2ae3d1cbceb). Exclusion and contamination rules in the preregistration were applied deterministically and no exclusions occurred in the confirmatory partition.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary counts. Execution completed as a confirmatory run: planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, model_calls_used = 251. Analysis produced the contingency table shown in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Aggregated condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) are baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996) and guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.004 (0.4 percentage points).

Statistical inference and uncertainty quantification. The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test returned p = 1.0 given the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0). The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval on the paired difference (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These exact numbers and the bootstrap settings are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha256 = 7bed98798cfd53d70c9a94a3fc742b9b5d3bb83a0f525630005c57b90146eb32).

Repair conversion and failure analysis. Only one repair call was exercised (stage_counts: repair = 1) and that single permitted repair converted the sole failing baseline candidate into a validator-pass in the guarded episode. Repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%). Contamination detectors and exclusion filters flagged no episodes in the confirmatory partition (analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty for this partition; sha256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Missingness_summary reports 250 complete pairs and zero failed episodes (analysis/missingness_summary.csv, sha256 = 2871565edf003706ee8c4b3eeb86a44d47e986c5aa8ef06b8ea322ebbf07eb07).

Representative artifacts. Representative task and response artifacts are archived and examples include the shared initial and per-condition response files for multiple tasks (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt sha256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080 and the corresponding scoring artifacts named above). Validator traces for passed episodes include normalized_configuration, final_state snapshots, parsed_command_count and required_command_count fields; a typical hard-difficulty task (task-000003) shows parsed_command_count = 6 and required_command_count = 6 in its validator trace (see execution/scoring/task-000003-*.json entries in the archive).
sections.discussion:
Practical interpretation. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and on the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was near-null: initial gpt-5-mini candidates already satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases, leaving only one candidate that the single allowed repair converted. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement under this pipeline and task scope.

Why the observed marginal effect is small. Artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed guarded gain: (1) the task generator constrained intents and limited allowed_touched_fields and required_sequences, reducing variation and making validator-consistent candidates easier to produce; (2) the model and preserved prompt templates reliably emitted well-formed CLI sequences for these constrained intents; (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties but does not measure broader live-protocol behavior. These constraints and their encoded policies are visible in task_manifest entries (e.g., allowed_fields, required_sequence and difficulty fields) in the archive.

Power, preregistration assumptions, and implications. The preregistration assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 for power planning; the realized baseline pass rate 0.996 substantially reduced power to detect small positive guarded effects. Thus the null or near-null paired-test result should be understood in context: our analysis reports exact p-values but the most informative practical statement is the paired-bootstrap CI on the maximum plausible verifier benefit under this task and model. Reporting exact counts, the bootstrap CI, and the repair-conversion numerator provides readers with the concrete bounds necessary to assess practical impact.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on the precise prompt templates, the single-repair policy, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the shared_initial_candidate design. Construct validity: the deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, workflow ordering) and does not assert behavioral correctness in live protocol operation or emergent interactions. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain open. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised in this run. Conclusion: while GVR guardrails conceptually reduce mechanically verifiable error classes, in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM their marginal validator-detected benefit may be limited — this does not imply guardrails are unnecessary in broader or adversarial operational contexts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration.

Preregistration and immutable prompt references (archived): preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1; preregistration artifact SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede. Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Key execution artifacts used for reconciliation and accounting: execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 = 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9; execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json sha256 = 91b0c6be4fb851deb73df0bd32462200fc3ead6715154abb2f387feee5f87de3. The evidence bundle contains the full execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and artifact hashes referenced in this manuscript.

Executed confirmatory estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). Provider-call accounting in the archive reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) and stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate design. Full execution and analysis manifests and per-artifact hashes are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
